name: Is port {{port}} in use?
description: Shows what is listening on a port, and the process that owns it. Prompts for the port when you run it.
author: voltius

snippets.name: Is port {{port}} in use?
snippets.description: Falls back from ss to lsof to netstat, so it works on a minimal host.

steps.content:
PORT="{{port:number}}"

# $PORT is embedded in a regex (netstat branch) and in tool-specific argument
# syntax (ss/lsof branches), so a non-numeric value is not just wrong, it can
# match unrelated ports or make the tool error out. Require plain digits before
# running any of the three detection branches.
case "$PORT" in
  ''|*[!0-9]*)
    echo "Not a valid port: '$PORT' (expected a number)"
    PORT_VALID=0
    ;;
  *)
    PORT_VALID=1
    ;;
esac

if [ "$PORT_VALID" = 1 ]; then
  if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    OUT=$(ss -tulpnH "sport = :$PORT" 2>/dev/null)
  elif command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    OUT=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:"$PORT" -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null; lsof -nP -iUDP:"$PORT" 2>/dev/null)
  else
    OUT=$(netstat -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep -E "[:.]$PORT[[:space:]]")
  fi

  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    echo "Port $PORT is IN USE:"
    echo "$OUT"
  else
    echo "Port $PORT is free (nothing listening)."
    echo "Note: without sudo you may not see sockets owned by other users."
  fi
fi
